section.title: Centering the patient
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Positioning the patient/Moving the patient to the scan start position/Checking the patient position/Centering the patient

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Centering the patient
1 For optimum image quality and dose application to patient size and body shape with CARE Dose4D, position the patient in the isocenter of the gantry.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30
6 Examination
2 Double-check and verify the position of the patient with the laser lightmarker as well as in the topogram.
If the patient is positioned too high, the mAs for the subsequent scan is increased.
If the patient is positioned too low, the mAs for the subsequent scan is reduced and the images show increased noise.
For head scans with Auto Isocenter, you may be prompted to raise or lower the patient table. This has no impact on the dose modulation with CARE Dose4D.

section.title: Positioning the patient for radiotherapy without automated zeroing
section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Positioning the patient/Radiotherapy functions/Positioning the patient for radiotherapy without automated zeroing

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Positioning the patient for radiotherapy without automated zeroing
Automated table zeroing is turned off.
The positioning screen has changed and the following icons are available:
Patient model
Save at RT Laser icon Saves the position at the external (RT) laser.
Move to RT Laser icon
Moves the patient table back to the external (RT) laser position.
External (RT) laser
1 Tap the Save at RT Laser icon to save the current table position at the external (RT) Laser and to activate the move request of the patient table.
The current table position at the external (RT) Laser is saved.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 302
6 Examination
2 Optional: Press and hold the Move key until movement stops.
The patient table moved to the internal (CT) Laser.
3 Optional: Zero the patient table at the internal CT Laser. Tap and hold the Horizontal zeroing icon.
4 Use the Table In/Out keys to move the patient table to the scan start position. You can now perform a scan.
5 Tap the Move to RT Laser icon.
6 Press and hold the Move key until the patient table has reached the saved position at the RT Laser.
The marks on the patient are lined up with the external laser lightmarker again.

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 6.5.1 Immobilizing animal patients
Sedate or anesthetize

Veterinary use of the SOMATOM CT system requires that you sedate or anesthetize the animal patient before scanning. This is done to prevent injury to the animal patient or attending personnel, damage to the equipment, or misdiagnosis due to movement of the animal patient during scanning.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 304
6 Examination
CAUTION
The animal is not immobilized!
Contusion, fractures of the operator, personnel or attendant. Damage to the equipment.
◆ Always anesthetize or sedate the animal before scanning.
◆ Keep the number of persons in the examination room as low as possible.
CAUTION
The animal is not immobilized!
Wrong diagnosis due to wrong image information.
◆ Always anesthetize or sedate the animal before scanning.
Movement during scanning

If the effect of the sedation or anesthetization weakens during scanning, uncontrolled movements of the animal patient could also result in injury or misdiagnosis. Therefore the animal patient needs to be observed at all times.
CAUTION
Unintentional patient movement!
Injury to the patient.
◆ Always fix and observe the patient during the measurement.
WARNING
Incorrect patient positioning, unintended patient movement, and unobserved movement of the patient table or gantry!
Injury to the patient, for example, contusions of the patient's extremities and unusable radiation.
◆ Always fix the patient with accessories, as described in the instructions for use, to avoid unintentional patient movement. For example, use restraint straps and arm supports.

◆ Monitor the patient continuously as long as the table top and gantry are moving. Take special care if the tilt of the gantry is anything other than zero degrees or the table height is anything other than the isocenter.

◆ Make sure that nothing can get caught while the table or gantry are moving. For example, parts of the body or clothing, any needles, infusion tubes, respiration tubes, catheters, ECG cables, or sheets and blankets.
◆ Follow the markings and labels on the equipment.
◆ Press a STOP key if an injury to the patient can occur.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 305

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Starting the topogram scan
If you have a scan room door observation, a yellow message is displayed after you have loaded the scan protocol, and the door of the examination room is not closed.
A transparent blue shutter is displayed on the topogram, which indicates the available FoV. It is shown when the corresponding tomogram scan entry is selected.
The area where image quality prevails is inside the blue shutter, and needs to be kept in mind for patient positioning:
Cardiac, Chest Pain, Obese, and Heart VPCT: The blue shutters in the resulting topogram indicate the parts with reduced temporal resolution.
Turbo Flash Spiral, Turbo Flash Thorax, Turbo Flash Spiral Cardiac: The blue shutter in the resulting topogram indicates the part that cannot be reconstructed.
Dual Energy: The blue shutter in the resulting topogram indicates that the outer part is reconstructed only with tube A.
Head and UHR: The blue shutter in the resulting topogram indicates the part that cannot be reconstructed.
To achieve the required images, it is necessary to position the patient correctly.
1 When positioning the patient, zero the table position at the gantry or on the topogram Routine parameter card in a way that future table positions always refer to this position.
2 Click the Load button to confirm the scan parameters.
3 Press the START key on the control box.
The topogram and the CARE Profile are displayed in the upper left segment of the Examination task card.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 309
6 Examination
The CARE Profile shows the distribution of the dose to be applied along the z-axis of the patient for the selected scan range.
In the topogram, two dashed orange lines are displayed. These lines delimitate the area in which the patient may be exposed to radiation for the tomogram scan.
The topogram is displayed in real time. You can stop the scan with the Suspend button as soon as enough data is acquired.
4 On the Routine parameter card, adjust the table position stepwise, if necessary.
You have to pay special attention while moving the patient table to avoid any risk of injury to the patient.

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Checking parameter settings
Examination direction
Table position (horizontal/vertical)
Examination range
Comment lines
Number of scans and images
Slice thickness
Time settings
Radiation parameters
The Scan parameter card contains further parameter settings for scanning.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30
6 Examination
CAUTION
Changed scan parameters are unsuitable!
Dose not as desired.
◆ Verify the changed scan parameters before scanning.
◆ On the Routine parameter card, check the default scan parameters, and adapt them if necessary.
For certain sequence scan protocols, the values in the No. of scans and Feed fields are adapted automatically and, therefore, are not editable.

Certain modes of operation allow selections of scan parameters that may lead to a peripheral CTDI100 of more than 1 Gy. This dose may exceed the threshold for deterministic radiation effects on the patient's skin or eye lenses. For information on dose reduction techniques, see: ( Page 189 Dose management and optimization). For general dose information on the CT system, see: System Owner Manual .

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Performing the spiral acquisition
After you changed scan parameters, you must confirm the new settings with Load before starting the scan.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30
6 Examination
If the spiral is part of an auto range and not all ranges have been selected at least once, a parameter overview is displayed. You can display this overview manually with View
> Examination Overview... .
1 Click the Load button to confirm the scan parameters.
As soon as you click the Load button, the topogram is zoomed and moved in a way that the whole planned scan range is displayed.
2 Press the MOVE key on the control box until table movement stops.
– or –
Click the Cancel Move button to begin the spiral at the current table position.
3 Press the START key on the control box.
You can observe the progress of your scan on the screen:
In the chronicle, you can see the remaining scan time.
In the topogram, the current scan position is displayed.
In the tomo segment, the calculated tomograms are displayed.
RTD (Real Time Display) images are reconstructed to observe the scan progress.
4 Use the MOVE key to move to the starting position of the next range.
5 Begin with the next scan.
– or –
Reconstruct the scan series with full image quality.
Force / Force Velo | Instructions for Use Print No. C2-058-C.621.01.01.02
SOMATOM | syngo CT VB30 319
6 Examination
6 Conclude the examination by creating a topographic image. For how to proceed: ( Page 326 Reconstruction), ( Page 331 Concluding an Examination)

section.hierarchy_path: /Examination/Scan/Acquiring an Adaptive 4D spiral/Displaying the Cycle time table dialog box

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 6 Examination
Displaying the Cycle time table dialog box
You can define different cycle times for one Adaptive 4D Spiral scan in the Cycle time table dialog box.
1 Click the Activate cycle time table icon on the Scan parameter card.
The Cycle time entry changes to Multiple .
2 Right-click the Edit cycle time table icon.
The Cycle time table dialog box is displayed.
You can use the cycle time table also for certain scan protocols without table feed, for example, non-gated perfusion sequence scans.

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Performing acquisition
After you changed scan parameters, you must confirm the new settings with Load before starting the scan.
1 Click the Load button to confirm the scan parameters.
As soon as you click the Load button, the topogram is zoomed and moved in a way that the whole planned scan range is displayed.
2 Press the MOVE key on the control box until table movement stops.
– or –
Click the Cancel Move button to begin the spiral at the current table position.
3 Press the START key on the control box.
You can observe the progress of your scan on the screen:
In the chronicle, you can see the remaining scan time.
In the topogram, the current scan position is displayed.
In the tomo segment, the calculated tomograms are displayed.
RTD (Real Time Display) images are reconstructed to observe the scan progress.
4 Reconstruct the scan series with full image quality at the end of scanning.
5 Conclude the examination by creating a topographic image. For how to proceed: ( Page 326 Reconstruction), ( Page 331 Concluding an Examination)

section.hierarchy_path: /Enhanced examination/CARE Contrast CT/Activating the coupled mode/Setting the coupled mode/Autoranges in coupled mode

semantic_nodes.canonical_text: Autoranges in coupled mode
In an autorange, select the Injector coupled setting for the first scan range only. The injector is automatically coupled for all remaining ranges.
If you suspend the scan in an autorange, the injection is canceled immediately for the current scan range.
